title: Surface stale reference-data values on Amend pages
summary: When a stored answer's country or port code has dropped out of the current reference-data list (an MDM re-release), the page's GET handler now blanks the stale value, adds a 'no longer available' error, and leaves the stored answer untouched so Save-and-continue cannot silently overwrite it with a blank. Landed on six animals pages (322f8b01) and two plants pages plus an investigation-only pinning commit (62a32ef, 31684a0, c69acf0, 2eaa7e4, 696c5e8, a918b7f). Every touched file — controllers, controller tests, copy pairs — is either untouched by the alignment branch or touched only on an unrelated single line (the `const view` template-path rename), so every file in this cluster merges cleanly with no manual resolution needed. The branch never touches either journey's `services/countries` or `services/ports` (s19's countries-lazy-load stage is scoped to ins only; s12/s18 do not reach these service files), so the `originCountries()` / `ports.list()` / `ports.portOptions()` calls this fix relies on are byte-identical before and after the merge and the fix's behaviour is unaffected by the alignment.

branchEquivalent.evidence: The branch carries no equivalent stale-reference-data behaviour on either journey. Its only interaction with this cluster's files is s21's one-line `const view` template-path rename in three of the six animals controllers, and no interaction at all with the plants files. The branch's countries/ports services (services/countries/*, services/ports/*) are byte-identical to main's for both journeys — confirmed by an empty `git diff --stat` over both paths between each repo's merge-base and the branch — so the readers this fix depends on (originCountries(), ports.list(), ports.portOptions()) are unaffected.

verdictWhy: Every file in the cluster is either untouched by the branch or touched on a single, non-overlapping line (the s21 template rename). No manual conflict resolution is required anywhere in this cluster; a straight merge of main into the branch carries the fix through intact and it continues to call the same countries/ports functions with the same signatures.
behaviourChanges: No new behaviour change from the merge itself: the fix's runtime behaviour (blank the stale value, surface a 'no longer available' error, leave the stored answer intact) is identical before and after merging main into the branch, because the branch never touches services/countries, services/ports, or the business logic of any of the sixteen files this cluster spans.

Recorded scope boundary (not introduced by this merge, but worth carrying forward): only origin, import-reason, port-of-entry, private-transporter-details and transit-countries (animals) and origin and arrival-details (plants) scrub stale values on GET. The hub's Completed roll-up and the check-answers summary card do not cross-check a stale code against the current reader list — 62a32ef's three pinning tests document this as the investigation's own scope decision, not a gap this cluster's merge introduces or fixes.

openQuestions.question: Should the hub 'Completed' status and the check-answers summary card also warn when a stored answer's code has gone stale (the two pinned-but-unfixed surfaces from 62a32ef), or is GET-time scrubbing on the answer pages themselves judged sufficient coverage for EUDPA-573?
openQuestions.default: Leave as scoped — the investigation commit deliberately pins the current behaviour there rather than changing it, and no alignment stage touches those files, so there is nothing this merge forces a decision on.

claims.statement: Animals' origin controller detects staleness by checking the stored countryOfOrigin against countries.originCountries(), the same reader the alignment's s19 countries-lazy-load stage deliberately keeps ins from adopting (D4) and never touches on the journeys.

The branch's only change to three of the six animals controllers this cluster touches is the s21 feature-folder convention's one-line template-path rename, so the merge is a clean, non-overlapping 3-way merge.
The branch never touches either journey's services/countries or services/ports directories; the diff between each repo's merge-base and the branch over those paths is empty.
